accountRecipients.privacy.ownAccounts: Paying one of your own accounts is an ordinary Cardano payment: anyone can see the two accounts paying each other and tell they're one wallet's. Sending from your private balance instead would avoid that.
accountRecipients.title: Your accounts
accounts.customNote: A number of your own works too — 1338, say. The look above goes in order and stops at the first account never used, so it can't find one out on its own; checking it by number can. You can add an account that has never been used and start using it: it exists in your recovery phrase either way, and holds nothing until you put something there.
accounts.foundAccount: Found Account {{number}}. It's in the list now.
accounts.hasBeenUsed: Account {{number}} has been used on {{network}}. It's in the list now.
accounts.heading: Accounts
accounts.inListNow: Account {{number}} is in the list now.
accounts.neverUsed: Account {{number}} has never been used on {{network}}. You can still add it and start using it.
accounts.nextNeverUsed: The next account in order has never been used on {{network}}. A custom number may still have been: check one below.
accounts.note: Each account is a separate Cardano wallet from the same recovery phrase, with its own addresses, its own staking and its own collateral. Other wallets call these accounts too, and show the same ones for this phrase.
accounts.privacy.koiosCost: {{look}} and {{check}} each ask Koios about one account, and the wallet only ever asks about one at a time: asking about twenty at once would tell Koios those twenty accounts are one wallet's. {{add}} asks nobody anything.
accounts.privacy.sharedBalance: Your private balance is shared: there's one of it for the whole phrase, whichever account you're on. Nothing on chain links money you make private from one account to money you make private from another — but spending both in one private payment would, so the wallet keeps them apart and says so when it can't.
accounts.title: Public accounts
activity.export.privacy.private: The file isn't encrypted. Each row has its transaction's ID, so whoever has it can find every one on the chain. It ties your private payments, your private sessions and your Lovejoin boxes to each other and to your public account, and shows which Seedelf each payment went to. Give it only to someone you'd show all of that.
activity.export.privacy.public: The file isn't encrypted, though everything in it is on the chain anyway.
activity.export.readSoFar_one: It has the {{count}} transaction read so far: Load more first to include older ones.
activity.export.readSoFar_other: It has the {{count}} transactions read so far: Load more first to include older ones.
activity.export.title: Export
activity.fromKoios: Read from Koios, which already knows this account, 20 transactions at a time.
activity.noteWarning: Anyone can read a note on a transaction, and anyone can write one.
activity.privacy.kept: Kept encrypted on this device, never asked of Koios. It starts from when this wallet first saw each payment.
adaInput.leastInPayment: {{amount}} ₳ is the least ADA the network accepts in a payment.
adaInput.leastWithTokens: {{amount}} ₳ is the least ADA the network accepts with these tokens.
adaInput.minimumHint: Leave it empty and the tokens go with only the ADA they need. The review shows how much.
app.name: Seedelf Wallet
claim.aside: Each session in its own transaction. Nothing is sent until you press Send
claim.privacy.directly: They come back directly, as you chose: anyone can tie each on chain to its session and its funding.
claim.privacy.ownTransactions: Each session comes back in its own transaction, so nothing in them ties the sessions together. They're sent one after another, though, and returns that land together hint that they're one person's.
claim.privacy.throughLovejoin: A session's spare ADA goes through Lovejoin first, paid by that session, and each box comes back on its own, later. But their deposits land in the same block or two and their mixes share blocks, and a pool with few boxes serves the first sessions while the rest come back directly. Bringing each back from its own page, hours apart, avoids both.
claim.result.note: Each lands within a minute or two. A site's session stays connected, to an empty account, until you disconnect it.
claim.result.title: Coming back
claim.tapToLeaveOut: Tap a session to leave it out
claim.title: Bring everything back
claim.warn.lovejoinSkipped_one: Lovejoin is left out of one return, which comes back directly:
claim.warn.lovejoinSkipped_other: Lovejoin is left out of some returns, which come back directly:
collateral.candidate: Your account holds a UTxO of exactly 5 ₳, which can be the collateral with no transaction.
collateral.note: Collateral is 5 ₳ of your public account set aside for transactions that run a smart contract, such as creating a Seedelf from your account. It's only taken if the contract fails, which the wallet checks before sending, and it's kept out of your payments.
collateral.privacy.giveme: Payments from your private balance never put it up: giveme.my lends its own, so nothing on chain ties them to your account. giveme.my is run by Logical Mechanism, who make Seedelf Wallet, and it sees each of those payments, with your IP address.
collateral.reclaimed: You reclaimed it, so the wallet doesn't set one by itself.
collateral.review.note: Once the network confirms it, in about a minute, this 5 ₳ is your collateral. Only the fee leaves your account.
collateral.review.title: Review the collateral
collateral.setBy.wallet: The wallet: a 5 ₳ UTxO your account held
collateral.waiting: Waiting for the network to confirm the payment that sets it
collateral.warn.reclaiming: Reclaiming returns it to your balance. The wallet then won't set one by itself: set it again here when you want one.
collateral.willPaySelf: Setting it pays 5 ₳ from your public account to itself: only the network fee leaves it.
contacts.empty: No contacts yet. Save a Seedelf or an address you pay often, then pick it in Send or Make public.
contacts.noneOfKind: No contacts of this kind yet.
contacts.privacy.encrypted: Contacts are encrypted on this device, and can't be read while the wallet is locked.
contacts.title: Contacts
create.confirm.enterWords: Enter words {{words}} from your written copy.
create.confirm.title: Confirm your phrase
create.phrase.note: Write these 24 words on paper, in order, and keep it somewhere safe. They are the only way to restore this wallet. Anyone who has them can take your funds.
create.phrase.onlyHere: This phrase restores your Seedelfs only in Seedelf Wallet. Other Cardano wallets will show your public account and nothing else.
create.phrase.title: Your recovery phrase
create.phrase.warn.neverCopy: Don't copy the phrase into a screenshot, a chat, an email or a cloud note, and never type it into a website.
create.wordMismatch: Word {{number}} doesn't match. Check your written copy.

destination.privacy.hintSeedelf: A Cardano address, an ADA Handle like $name, or a Seedelf's whole name. Looking up a handle tells Koios which one.
explorer.warning.account: Opening this on Cardanoscan tells that site, and your browser history, that this account is yours.
explorer.warning.transaction: Opening this on Cardanoscan tells that site, and your browser history, that this transaction is yours.
explorer.warning.transactions: Opening these on Cardanoscan tells that site, and your browser history, that these transactions are yours.
format.ada.notANumber: Enter an amount in ADA, like 25 or 12.5.
format.ada.tooMuch: That's more than all the ADA there is: 45 billion ₳.
format.ada.tooPrecise: ADA has at most 6 decimal places (0.000001 ₳ is one lovelace), so the extra digits were dropped.
format.commaNote: Use a point for decimals, like 12.5. A comma only groups thousands, like 1,000.
handleWarning.note_one: {{names}} is an ADA Handle. In a private balance, anyone who pays it from another wallet pays the Seedelf contract with nothing to say whose the payment is, so anyone can take it. Keep handles in a public account.
handleWarning.note_other: {{names}} are ADA Handles. In a private balance, anyone who pays one from another wallet pays the Seedelf contract with nothing to say whose the payment is, so anyone can take it. Keep handles in a public account.
handleWarning.returning_one: {{names}} is an ADA Handle, and this return brings it into your private balance. In a private balance, anyone who pays it from another wallet pays the Seedelf contract with nothing to say whose the payment is, so anyone can take it. Once it's back, make it public to your public account.
handleWarning.returning_other: {{names}} are ADA Handles, and this return brings them into your private balance. In a private balance, anyone who pays one from another wallet pays the Seedelf contract with nothing to say whose the payment is, so anyone can take it. Once they're back, make them public to your public account.
histories.kind.unknownMany: money from {{count}} transactions the wallet has no history for
histories.kind.unknownOne: money the wallet has no history for
histories.privacy.accounts: It spends money you made private from {{accounts}}, so anyone can tie those accounts to each other.
histories.privacy.lovejoinUndone_one: , and undoes some of what Lovejoin did for the box

histories.privacy.sessions_one: It spends money that {{sessions}} left, so anyone can tie that session to this one.

lock.idle: Nothing has been clicked or typed for a while.
lockFailed.warn.message: The wallet couldn't lock: {{message}} Try again. Closing the browser always locks it: it forgets your keys when it closes.
mint.costNote: About 1.75 ₳ stays locked with the Seedelf, and the network fee is about 0.25 ₳. The review shows the exact amounts.
mint.listedAs: Listed as {{tag}}, with a token name starting
mint.listedNoTag: With no tag, it's listed by its token name alone, starting
mint.note: A Seedelf is a name you can give out. Anyone can pay it, and each payment reaches you under a fresh copy of your register, so payments can't be linked to each other or to you.
mint.privacy.fromAccount: The Seedelf is linked to your public account openly. Money you make private afterwards isn't tied to it: making money private looks the same as paying anyone's Seedelf. So create your Seedelf before making money private.
mint.privacy.fromPrivate: A stealth mint. It only keeps the Seedelf apart from your public account when your private balance came from other people's Seedelf payments. Money you made private yourself can be traced back to the account.
mint.review.noteAccount: Send submits it. It takes about a minute for the network to confirm. Only removing the Seedelf gives back the ADA locked with it.
mint.review.notePrivate: Send asks giveme.my to lend the collateral, then submits. It takes about a minute for the network to confirm. Only removing the Seedelf gives back the ADA locked with it.
mint.review.title: Review the new Seedelf
mint.tagRules: . Up to {{max}} letters, digits, spaces or ASCII punctuation. Anyone can read it on chain.
moveIn.maxNote: Everything except the fee and what the tokens you keep need. Your collateral and any UTxOs you locked stay put.
moveIn.maxNoteRewards: Everything except the fee and what the tokens you keep need, staking rewards included. Your collateral and any UTxOs you locked stay put.
moveIn.note: Move ADA, and any amount of your tokens, from your public account into your private balance.
moveIn.privacy.links: Making money private links your public account to the new private UTxOs, but not to any Seedelf name.
moveIn.review.note: The new UTxOs are locked to fresh copies of your Seedelf key's register. It takes about a minute for the network to confirm them.
moveIn.review.title: Review making it private
moveIn.tooMuch: That's more than the {{amount}} ₳ available in your public account.
network.label: Network
network.mainnet: Mainnet: Cardano's real network. ADA here is real money.
network.privacy.preprod: Preprod: Cardano's test network, for trying the wallet out with a recovery phrase you don't use on mainnet: the same phrase has the same keys on both networks, so anyone comparing them can tell they're one wallet's. ADA here is test ADA, with no value.
network.testStrip: Preprod, Cardano's test network: ADA here is test ADA, with no value.
pool.warn.oversaturated: This pool is oversaturated: every delegator's rewards shrink.
pool.warn.retired: This pool has retired: it earns nothing now. Choose another.
pool.warn.retiring: This pool retires in epoch {{epoch}}: choose another before then.
pool.warn.underPledged: Its owners stake less than they pledged, so the pool earns no rewards until they make it up.
pools.firstDeposit: Staking the first time takes a 2 ₳ deposit, which comes back when you stop.
pools.row.sharedTicker: , a ticker other pools use too
pools.warn.sharedTicker: {{count}} live pools use this ticker, or one that looks the same. Anyone can register a pool under any ticker: only the pool ID tells them apart. Check it against the one the pool publishes before you stake.
receive.address.label: Receive address
receive.handles.note_one: A wallet paying this handle pays the address holding it: this account. A handle is as public as the address.
receive.handles.note_other: A wallet paying one of these pays the address holding it: this account. A handle is as public as the address.
receive.handles.title: Your ADA Handles
receive.note.fund: Anything that can pay a Cardano address can fund this wallet: scan the code from a phone wallet, or copy the address.
receive.privacy.publicAddress: This is an ordinary Cardano address: anyone can see what it receives. To be paid privately, give out one of your Seedelfs' names instead.
receive.privacy.seedelfName: A Seedelf's name is public, and linked to whatever paid to create it. What's paid to it isn't.
receive.qr.label: QR code of the receive address
receive.seedelfs.locked: Locked with it: Remove gives it back
receive.seedelfs.none: People pay a Seedelf's name, and you don't have a Seedelf yet. Create one first: your public account pays for it.
receive.seedelfs.note: Give out a Seedelf's whole name: tags aren't unique. Anyone with Seedelf Wallet can pay it, and nobody can tell the payment is yours.
receive.seedelfs.title: Your Seedelfs
receive.stake.label: Stake address
receive.title: Receive
recipients.atMost: A payment pays at most {{number}} recipients.
remove.chooseWhere: Choose where the freed ADA goes
remove.note: Removing burns the Seedelf's token and frees the ADA locked with it, less the fee. Payments already sent to it stay yours; after this, nobody can pay it by name.
remove.privacy.backToAccount: Back where this Seedelf's ADA came from: {{whose}} paid for it, so this links nothing new.
remove.privacy.backToPrivate: Back where this Seedelf's ADA came from: your private balance paid for it, so this links nothing new.
remove.privacy.maybeAccountPaid: This links nothing new only if your public account paid for this Seedelf. If your private balance did, it ties the account to the Seedelf's name, and through the mint to the private UTxOs that paid for it.
remove.privacy.maybePrivatePaid: For a Seedelf you minted from your private balance. For one your public account paid for, this ties the Seedelf's name to the new UTxO, and to whatever it's later spent with.
remove.privacy.unknownPayer: Choose where the freed ADA goes. This wallet doesn't know who paid for this Seedelf, as when it was minted in another browser or before a restore. Send it back to the side that paid, so it links nothing new.
remove.review.note: The token is burned. Send asks giveme.my to lend the collateral, then submits. It takes about a minute for the network to confirm.
remove.review.title: Review the removal
remove.title: Remove {{name}}
remove.warn.accountPaid: Your public account paid for this Seedelf. Sending its ADA to your private balance ties the Seedelf's name, and so your account, to the new UTxO, and to whatever it's later spent with.
remove.warn.otherAccount: Account {{paid}} paid for this Seedelf, and the wallet is on Account {{active}}. The mint already links the Seedelf's name to the account that paid, so sending its ADA here links this account to that name as well — and anyone can tie your two accounts together through it. Switch to Account {{paid}} first, or send it to your private balance instead.
remove.warn.privatePaid: Your private balance paid for this Seedelf. Sending its ADA to your public account ties the account to the Seedelf's name, and through the mint to the private UTxOs that paid for it and their change.
reset.note: Without the password, the only way back in is your recovery phrase. This deletes the wallet from this browser, then you restore it from the phrase and choose a new password. The phrase brings back your public account, your private balance and your Lovejoin boxes. What private sessions' one-time accounts hold doesn't show after a restore yet. If a payment may still go through, an encrypted record of it stays in this browser: restoring this same phrase here watches it again, and making or restoring another wallet deletes that record.
reset.title: Restore from your phrase
reset.warn.noPhrase: If you don't have your recovery phrase, stop here. Deleting the wallet without it loses your funds for good.
restore.note: Enter your recovery phrase. A phrase from Lace, Eternl or Yoroi also works: its first account becomes this wallet's public account.
restore.pasteTip: Tip: paste the whole phrase into any box.
restore.title: Restore a wallet
review.nothingSent: Nothing is sent until you press Send
send.note.label: Note (optional)
send.note.privacy.hint: {{used}}/{{max}}. Anyone can read it, for good.
send.note.privacy.hintSeedelf: {{used}}/{{max}}. Anyone can read it, for good, and it could say whose Seedelf this pays.
send.privacy.open: This pays from your public account in the open: anyone can see it came from you. To pay without that link, make the money private and send it from there.
send.privacy.openSeedelf: This pays from your public account in the open: anyone can see it came from you and went to a private balance, though not whose. To pay without that link, make the money private and send it from there.
send.privacy.openSeedelfSeveral: This pays from your public account in the open: anyone can see it came from you and went to a private balance, though not whose. Paying several at once also shows they were paid together. To pay without that link, make the money private and send it from there.
send.privacy.openSeveral: This pays from your public account in the open: anyone can see it came from you. Paying several at once also shows they were paid together. To pay without that link, make the money private and send it from there.
send.privacy.otherAccount: This is your own Account {{number}}. It's an ordinary Cardano payment, so anyone can see your two accounts paying each other and tell they're one wallet's. Sending from your private balance instead would avoid that.
send.review.confirmTime: It takes about a minute for the network to confirm.
send.review.onlyOwnerEach: Only the owner of each Seedelf can spend the payment, and it can't be linked to their Seedelf by looking at the chain.
send.review.onlyOwnerThis: Only the owner of this Seedelf can spend the payment, and it can't be linked to their Seedelf by looking at the chain.
send.warn.ownAccount: This is your own public account: the payment comes back to it, less the fee.
serviceAccess.stillRefused: Chrome still isn't letting the wallet reach Koios.
serviceAccess.warn.blocked: Chrome isn't letting Seedelf Wallet reach Koios, where it reads Cardano, so your balances can't load and nothing can be sent. That happens when the wallet's site access is limited in Chrome's extension settings.
setPassword.hint.fair: Fair. A few more characters or words would help.
setPassword.hint.weak: Weak. Longer is stronger: a few random words work well.
setPassword.note: The password unlocks the wallet in this browser. It encrypts your recovery phrase here; it can't recover your funds anywhere else. Use at least {{min}} characters.
settings.check.match: That's this wallet's recovery phrase. Keep that copy somewhere safe and offline.
settings.check.note: Type the words from where you wrote them down, to make sure that copy restores this wallet. The wallet only says whether they match. Nothing is saved.
settings.check.warn.noMatch: That isn't this wallet's recovery phrase. Check each word against your copy; if it's wrong, write the phrase down again from Show recovery phrase.
settings.closingLocks: Closing the browser always locks it.
settings.currency.label: Show ADA's value in
settings.currency.mainnetOnly: Values show on mainnet only: test ADA has no price, so nothing is asked on preprod.
settings.currency.privacy.coingecko: From CoinGecko, read when Home opens, at most every five minutes. It learns only that someone at your IP address uses the wallet: nothing about what you hold.
settings.currency.privacy.none: No prices: the wallet asks CoinGecko nothing.
settings.language.label: Language
settings.language.warn.unchecked: Every language is in the wallet already: choosing one asks nobody anything. Spanish and Japanese have not been checked by a native speaker, so a warning may read oddly — English is always here to compare against.
settings.lovejoin.delayNote: A box comes back some minutes into the first time the wallet is unlocked after its wait: never the moment you unlock, nor right after the wallet sends something else.
settings.lovejoin.floor: The wallet mixes only once Lovejoin's pool holds {{count}} boxes that aren't yours; until then a return comes back directly, and says so.
settings.lovejoin.note: When a private session comes back with ADA to spare (a token→ADA swap's proceeds count), that ADA goes through Lovejoin first, in boxes of 10 ₳ mixed with other people's, so what comes back is harder to tie to the session on chain. The session pays for the mixes, and about 0.3 ₳ brings each box back. Its mixes are sent only while the wallet is unlocked: locking partway stops them, and what's left comes back directly. A swap or a mix brings it back by itself; a site's session, or a return you sent from Bring everything back, keeps it at its account until you bring it back.
settings.lovejoin.privacy.returnsOff: Off, a session's ADA comes back directly: anyone can tie it on chain to the session, and through its funding to the private UTxOs that paid for it. Your public account stays out either way. It saves each box's mixes ({{cost}}), about 0.3 ₳ to bring it back, and the hours of waiting. A mix from the Lovejoin tile still mixes, and a swap comes back as its approval said.
settings.lovejoin.returns: Bring private sessions back through Lovejoin
settings.lovejoin.returnsOn: A swap's approval, its Stop and each return you review can still bring that one back directly.
settings.moveToMainnet: Mainnet is Cardano's real network: ADA there is real money. Check every address and amount before you send.
settings.network.carriesOn: Anything on its way on {{network}} (a swap, Lovejoin, a payment) carries on there. A site asking something now is declined.
settings.openIn.panelNote: The toolbar button opens the wallet beside the page you're on, and it stays open as you browse.
settings.openIn.tabNote: The toolbar button opens the wallet in a tab, or brings back the one already open.
settings.openIn.useButton: Open it with the toolbar button.
settings.password.changed: Password changed. Use the new one to unlock from now on.
settings.phrase.enterPassword: Enter your password to see the words that restore this wallet. Check nobody can see your screen.
settings.phrase.title: Your recovery phrase
settings.phrase.warn.anyone: Anyone who has these words can take your funds. Don't copy them into a screenshot, a chat, an email or a cloud note, and never type them into a website.
settings.privacy.eachSeesIp: Each of them sees your IP address. Koios sends every transaction, from the same IP address that reads your public account.
settings.privacy.giveme: giveme.my is run by Logical Mechanism, who make Seedelf Wallet: to lend its collateral, it sees each payment from your private balance.
settings.privacy.moveToPreprod: Preprod is Cardano's test network. ADA there is test ADA, with no value: it can't pay for anything, and real ADA sent to a preprod address is lost. Your wallet is the same there, with its own balances, history and connected sites, and the same keys: anyone comparing the two networks can tell they're one wallet's. To keep them apart, test with a recovery phrase you don't use on mainnet.
settings.privacy.talksTo: The wallet only ever talks to Koios and giveme.my, and to Minswap when you swap. It has no accounts, analytics or tracking.
settings.privacy.talksToPrices: The wallet only ever talks to Koios and giveme.my, to CoinGecko for ADA's price, and to Minswap when you swap. It has no accounts, analytics or tracking.
settings.remove.anyway: Remove it anyway, leaving that behind
settings.remove.chainSending: {{network}}: a chain through Lovejoin is still being sent. Removing the wallet stops it partway, its boxes less mixed.
settings.remove.leftBehind: {{network}}: something no return takes is left at the account of {{names}}, and it doesn't show after a restore yet.
settings.remove.maybeSent: {{network}}: a payment Koios didn't answer may still go through. An encrypted record of it stays in this browser: restoring this same recovery phrase here watches it again, but making or restoring another wallet here first deletes that record. While nothing watches it, a payment made here or elsewhere could pay twice.
settings.remove.mixMaybeSent: {{network}}: a mix from your public account stopped at a transaction that may have gone through. An encrypted record of it stays in this browser: restoring this same recovery phrase here looks for it again before another mix from the account is built, but making or restoring another wallet here first deletes that record. While nothing looks for it, the account could pay for a mix twice.
settings.remove.note: This deletes the wallet from this browser. Your funds stay on the chain: your recovery phrase brings back your public account, your private balance and your Lovejoin boxes, here or in Seedelf Wallet on another device. What private sessions' one-time accounts hold doesn't show after a restore yet: bring it back first.
settings.remove.sessionsOpen_one: {{network}}: {{count}} private session still open: {{names}}. What its one-time account holds doesn't show after a restore yet: bring it back first, with Bring everything back on the dApps page, or a running swap's Stop.
settings.remove.sessionsOpen_other: {{network}}: {{count}} private sessions still open: {{names}}. What their one-time accounts hold doesn't show after a restore yet: bring it back first, with Bring everything back on the dApps page, or a running swap's Stop.
settings.remove.unreadable: {{network}}: Seedelf Wallet couldn't read what's still open there.
settings.remove.warn.cannotCheck: Seedelf Wallet couldn't check what's still open, which removing it would leave behind.
settings.remove.warn.havePhrase: Make sure you have your recovery phrase first (Show recovery phrase). Without it, removing the wallet loses your funds for good.
settings.remove.warn.stillOpen: Still open, which removing the wallet leaves behind:
settings.sites.connector: Let sites connect to Seedelf Wallet
settings.sites.password: Ask for your password to sign for a site
settings.sites.passwordOn: A site's transaction or message is signed only once you type your password, even while the wallet is unlocked.
settings.sites.privacy.account: Connected sites always use this account, whichever one you're working on, so switching accounts never shows a site a second account of yours. Changing it here shows every connected site the new account instead — which anyone watching both can see is the same wallet.
settings.sites.privacy.off: Off: sites can't see Seedelf Wallet. Turning it on asks Chrome to let the wallet add itself to https sites, as other Cardano wallets do. Then every https site you open, and scripts on it, can see that you use Seedelf Wallet, even sites you never connect (not your addresses or balance until you connect).
settings.sites.privacy.on: Sites find Seedelf Wallet as a Cardano wallet (CIP-30) and can ask to connect. When one asks, you choose what it sees: your public account, or a private session. Nothing is signed without you. Every https site you open, and scripts on it, can see that you use Seedelf Wallet, even one you never connect: not your addresses or balance until you connect it.
settings.sites.warn.blocked: Off, and it stays off in this version of Chrome: it can't keep websites away from the wallet's storage, where your encrypted wallet is. Update Chrome to let sites connect.
settings.sites.warn.passwordOff: Sign is enough while the wallet is unlocked, so anyone at your unlocked browser could sign for a site.
settings.staking.rewardsSpend: Anything your public account pays (a send, making money private, a Seedelf) withdraws the rewards too.
settings.staking.rewardsWait: Rewards wait until you withdraw them on the Staking page.
sites.disconnectText: {{site}} has to ask again before it sees anything more. It keeps what it already saw.
sites.disconnectTextSession: Private session {{number}} ends, and {{site}} has to ask again before it sees anything more. It keeps what it already saw. The wallet stops reading the session's account: anything the site pays it later, or leaves open on it, isn't looked for again.
sites.empty: No site is connected. A site asks when it wants to, and you choose.
sites.note: A disconnected site has to ask again before it sees anything more, and it keeps what it already saw. A private session is disconnected once everything in it is brought back, from the dApps page.
sites.title: Connected sites
staking.delegateFirstStop: Delegate your voting power first: stopping withdraws the rewards
staking.depositNote: The first time takes a 2 ₳ deposit, which comes back when you stop.
staking.note: Stake your public account with a pool to earn rewards every epoch (5 days). Your ADA stays in your account, free to spend.
staking.privacy.namesAccount: This is public: it names your public account.
staking.privacy.public: Staking and voting are public: anyone can see which pool and DRep your public account chose. Private money can't be staked: it has no staking part, so it earns nothing while it's private.
staking.review.depositNote: Registering your account to stake takes the deposit. Stopping staking gives it back.
staking.review.rewardsStart: Rewards start after about 15 to 20 days (the network takes a snapshot, then pays out an epoch later), then come every 5 days.
staking.review.stopNote: Your pool and your voting power's delegation end, and no more rewards come.
staking.rewardsSpent: Spent along with anything your public account pays, or withdrawn here. Settings can keep them here instead.
staking.rewardsWait: They wait here until you withdraw them: Settings keeps them out of your payments.
staking.title: Staking
staking.voteNote: Your stake has a say in Cardano's governance, through a DRep who votes for you.
staking.warn.rewardsLocked: Your {{amount}} ₳ of rewards can't be withdrawn until you delegate your voting power: to a DRep, or always abstain.
staking.warn.sharedDrepName: {{shared}}: only the ID above tells them apart.
startup.reloadNote: Reloading closes the wallet's windows. Your wallet is kept; you unlock it again with your password.
startup.title: The wallet couldn't start
token.amount.atMostDecimals: Enter an amount with at most {{decimals}} decimal places.
token.amount.tooMuch: That's more than the {{amount}} {{label}} you hold.
token.amount.tooMuchPlain: That's more than the {{amount}} you hold.
token.amount.tooPrecise: {{label}} has at most {{decimals}} decimal places, so the extra digits were dropped.
token.amount.wholeUnits: {{label}} comes in whole units, so the decimals were dropped.
token.showing: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}}. Search to narrow them down.
tokenList.notListed: Not in the wallet's token list, so its name is only what the token calls itself. Its policy ID is what identifies it.
transfer.pasteName: Paste the whole name the recipient gave you. Tags aren't unique, so the name is what counts.
transfer.privacy.timing: Sending right after making money private is easy to match by timing: the two sit close together on chain.
transfer.review.noteEach: Only the owner of each Seedelf can spend the payment, and it can't be linked to their Seedelf by looking at the chain. Send asks giveme.my to lend the collateral, then submits. It takes about a minute for the network to confirm.
transfer.review.noteThis: Only the owner of this Seedelf can spend the payment, and it can't be linked to their Seedelf by looking at the chain. Send asks giveme.my to lend the collateral, then submits. It takes about a minute for the network to confirm.
transfer.tooMuch: That's more than the {{amount}} ₳ in your private balance.
transfer.warn.ownSeedelf: This Seedelf is yours. Paying it moves money in a circle and costs a fee.
transfer.warn.toSelf: This Seedelf is yours: the payment comes back to your private balance, less the fee.
transfer.warn.toSelfSeveral: One of these Seedelfs is yours: its payment comes back to your private balance, less the fee.
unlock.forgot: Forgot password? Restore from your phrase
unlock.title: Welcome back
unlock.waiting.more_one: {{origin}} and {{count}} other site are asking for Seedelf Wallet. Unlock to see what they ask.
unlock.waiting.more_other: {{origin}} and {{count}} other sites are asking for Seedelf Wallet. Unlock to see what they ask.
unlock.waiting.site: {{origin}} is asking for Seedelf Wallet. Unlock to see what it asks.
unlock.waiting.unknown: A site is waiting for Seedelf Wallet. Unlock to see what it asks.
unlock.warn.trap: The wallet's core stopped working, so the wallet locked itself and let go of your keys. Unlock it to carry on.
utxos.collateralNote: Your collateral: put up by transactions that run a script, and otherwise kept. Reclaim it in Settings, under Collateral.
utxos.holdsSeedelf: It holds one of your Seedelfs.
utxos.lock.lock: Lock: keep it out of payments
utxos.lock.locked: Locked: tap to spend it again
utxos.lockNote: Lock a UTxO to keep it out of every payment from this balance, Max included.
utxos.lockNoteSite: A site's transaction can't use a locked UTxO either: the wallet refuses to sign it.
utxos.mixHolding: A mix through Lovejoin is being sent from this account ({{sent}} of {{total}} sent). The UTxOs it spends, and its change, are held by the mix: they're left out here and from your balance until it's all sent.
utxos.onlyRemoveSpends: Only removing the Seedelf spends it.
utxos.privacy.cameFrom: Came from: {{history}}. Payments try to keep money with different histories apart, since spending them together ties them to each other, and say when they can't. Lock it to keep it out of payments altogether.
utxos.privacy.onlyThisWallet: Only this wallet can tell these are yours. Looking one up on an explorer tells that site which UTxO you care about.
utxos.state.locked: Locked: left out of every payment.
utxos.warn.someUnspendable_one: One UTxO here holds a reference script the wallet can't spend, marked Can't spend. Anyone can send one.
utxos.warn.someUnspendable_other: {{count}} UTxOs here hold a reference script the wallet can't spend, marked Can't spend. Anyone can send one.
utxos.warn.unspendablePrivate: It holds a reference script, which the wallet can't spend yet: no payment takes it, and it isn't counted in your private balance. It stays yours.
utxos.warn.unspendablePublic: It holds a reference script that Koios doesn't give the wallet, so the wallet can't price spending it: no payment takes it, Max included.
vote.abstain.text: Your stake sits out every vote.
vote.abstain.title: Always abstain
vote.alreadyThere: Your voting power already goes there
vote.drep.text: Someone who votes for you: search by name, or paste their DRep ID.
vote.drep.title: A DRep
vote.listNote_one: {{count}} DRep with a name, from the wallet's list of {{date}}: searching it asks no one. For one who registered since, paste the whole ID.
vote.listNote_other: {{count}} DReps with a name, from the wallet's list of {{date}}: searching it asks no one. For one who registered since, paste the whole ID.
vote.noConfidence.text: Your stake votes no confidence in the constitutional committee, every time.
vote.noConfidence.title: Always no confidence
vote.noneMatch: No DRep on the wallet's list matches “{{query}}”. Paste its whole ID instead.
vote.notRegistered: Your account isn't registered to stake yet: this registers it, with a 2 ₳ deposit that comes back when you stop.
vote.note: Cardano's governance votes on changes to the chain and on spending from its treasury. Your stake's voting power goes where you choose.
vote.privacy.public: Where your voting power goes is public, and it names your public account.
vote.row.sharedName: , a name another DRep uses too
vote.sharedName.listed: {{count}} DReps on the wallet's list use this name, or one that looks the same
vote.sharedName.unlisted_one: A DRep on the wallet's list uses this name, or one that looks the same, under another ID
vote.sharedName.unlisted_other: {{count}} DReps on the wallet's list use this name, or one that looks the same, each under another ID
vote.warn.inactive: This DRep hasn't voted lately, so its votes don't count until it does. Your rewards unlock either way.
vote.warn.sharedName: {{shared}}. Anyone can take any name: only the ID tells them apart. Check it against the one the DRep publishes before you delegate.
withdraw.leftLimit: a transaction takes {{max}} at most, and never a token adding up to more than one output can hold.
withdraw.leftTokens_one: it holds a token that would add up to more with the rest than one output can hold.
withdraw.leftTokens_other: each holds a token that would add up to more with the rest than one output can hold.
withdraw.left_one: {{count}} private UTxO stays for another payment:
withdraw.left_other: {{count}} private UTxOs stay for another payment:
withdraw.maxNote: Everything in your private balance, up to 20 UTxOs at once, with every token, less the fee. Spending them together ties them to each other.
withdraw.maxNoteLocked: Everything in your private balance, up to 20 UTxOs at once, with every token, less the fee. Spending them together ties them to each other. UTxOs you locked stay put.
withdraw.privacy.linksBack: Making money public where it came from links it back. Send it somewhere else, or keep it private.
withdraw.privacy.linksBackSeveral: Making money public where it came from links it back. Send it somewhere else, or keep it private. Addresses paid in one payment can be seen to be paid together.
withdraw.review.note: Send asks giveme.my to lend the collateral, then submits. It takes about a minute for the network to confirm.
withdraw.review.title: Review the payment
withdraw.warn.ownAccount: This is your own {{whose}}. Making money public here links it back to it, and to whoever made it private.
